angle-2.label: One Reassignment, Infinite Downstream Risk
angle-2.expansion: Every territory move you make by hand is a thread you pulled — and you won't know what unraveled until a rep disputes their Q3 payout.

angle-2.label: You Become the Commission System
angle-2.expansion: When there's no infrastructure to handle reassignment cleanly, the logic lives in your head. You're not running the process — you are the process.

angle-1.label: Perpetual Rebuild Tax
angle-1.expansion: Every reassignment shouldn't require you to tear down and reconstruct the entire comp structure. When it does, you're not running ops — you're doing damage control on a system that was never built to flex.

angle-1.label: No Clean Source of Truth
angle-1.expansion: When leadership asks who owned what account and when, you're piecing together a timeline from spreadsheet versions and memory. That's not a system — that's a liability you're carrying alone.

angle-1.label: Rep Trust on the Line
angle-1.expansion: Every misattributed deal or missed credit tied to a reassignment lands on you. Reps don't see the complexity — they see a paycheck that doesn't match what they were promised.

angle-2.label: Strategy Held Hostage
angle-2.expansion: You've aligned on the right comp structure. But the system can't execute it — so leadership sits on a decision that should already be live.

angle-2.label: Ops Owns the Delay
angle-2.expansion: The business is waiting on you — not because the thinking is wrong, but because the tooling can't keep up. You become the reason the change didn't happen.

angle-2.label: Dread as a Design Constraint
angle-2.expansion: When you scope a new comp structure around what the system can handle, the fear of implementation is already shaping what you're willing to propose.

angle-1.label: Loss of Control
angle-1.expansion: The plan is supposed to serve the business pivot. Instead, your spreadsheet decides what's possible. Leadership changes the strategy — you inherit the chaos.

angle-1.label: Scapegoat Risk
angle-1.expansion: When a rep gets paid on the old structure because a version wasn't propagated correctly, there's no audit trail proving when the change was made — just your name on the file.

angle-1.label: Competence Ceiling
angle-1.expansion: Every mid-year restructure exposes the same limit: your process can't keep up with the business. Leadership doesn't see the spreadsheet — they see an ops function that can't execute.

angle-1.label: History Becomes Your Problem
angle-1.expansion: When the plan changes mid-year, every prior period becomes a question mark you have to re-answer. You're not managing compensation — you're managing a restatement.

angle-1.label: No Defensible Source of Truth
angle-1.expansion: If someone audits attainment against the new structure, you have no clean record to point to. The plan changed, but the history didn't — and that gap is yours to explain.

angle-2.label: The Rebuild Is On You
angle-2.expansion: When leadership decides to backdate a change, the tool says no — so you become the workaround. Every hour you spend manually reconstructing history is an hour you're doing the system's job.

angle-2.label: You Own What You Can't Prove
angle-2.expansion: A retroactive change with no audit trail means you're the only record of what happened. If a rep disputes it, there's no versioned history to show — just your word against theirs.

angle-1.label: History Gets Rewritten
angle-1.expansion: When the original plan is gone, so is your proof. You can't defend what the plan said in January if March's version is the only one that exists.

angle-1.label: Scapegoat With No Receipt
angle-1.expansion: A rep disputes their Q1 payout under a plan that no longer exists on paper. You remember what it said. That's not the same as being able to show it.

angle-1.label: Reactive by Design
angle-1.expansion: Every mid-year change turns you into a cleanup crew. You're not forecasting the business — you're catching up to decisions Finance wasn't part of making.

angle-1.label: The Number You Can't Stand Behind
angle-1.expansion: When the accrual shifts mid-period, you're presenting a commission expense figure with an asterisk. Leadership sees a restatement — you see your credibility walking out the door.

angle-2.label: Approving Blind
angle-2.expansion: You're being asked to sign off on a comp change with no forward-looking cost model. That's not an approval — that's a guess with your name on it.

angle-2.label: Budget Integrity at Stake
angle-2.expansion: When accruals shift mid-year and the variance hits the P&L, Finance doesn't get to say they were surprised. You own the number — even when you never owned the decision.

angle-1.label: No Proof You Were Right
angle-1.expansion: When someone questions the number, you can't show your work. There's no record of what the plan said before the change — only what it says now.

angle-1.label: Reprocessing Owns You
angle-1.expansion: Every mid-year change sends you back to period one. The close isn't a finish line — it's just the start of another manual rebuild you have to run alone.

angle-2.label: Reconciliation Without Ground Truth
angle-2.expansion: When a retroactive change rewrites history, you're not reconciling numbers — you're reconstructing them. Every period you thought was closed quietly isn't.

angle-2.label: You Become the Audit
angle-2.expansion: There's no system of record, so the investigation is you — your time, your credibility, your name on a number you had to manually reverse-engineer.

angle-2.label: Version Chaos Credibility
angle-2.expansion: When a rep pulls up last month's plan doc and it doesn't match what you announced, you're not the source of truth anymore — you're the source of confusion.

angle-2.label: Change You Can't Prove
angle-2.expansion: You made the update, sent the email, held the call — but if there's no audit trail showing who saw what and when, you're one dispute away from owning a rollout you can't defend.

angle-1.label: Trust Collapsed Overnight
angle-1.expansion: You didn't change the relationship — a number did. But the rep doesn't see the system, they see you. You become the person who moved the goalposts.

angle-1.label: Math You Can't Defend
angle-1.expansion: The rep's dashboard says 74% attainment. Last week it said 91%. Nothing changed in their pipeline — only your decision did. Now you're explaining arithmetic instead of leading.

angle-1.label: Credibility Priced Into the Plan
angle-1.expansion: Every future comp announcement arrives with a shadow of doubt. You said the number once. Then you changed it. Reps stop trusting the plan — and they stop trusting you to protect them.

angle-2.label: The Math Owns You
angle-2.expansion: A promotion should be a moment you own. Instead, you're buried in a spreadsheet, reverse-engineering attainment history just to honor a decision that's already been made.

angle-2.label: One Wrong Carry, One Angry Rep
angle-2.expansion: If that carryforward is off by even a percentage point, the rep who just got promoted is the first one to notice — and you're the one explaining it.

angle-1.label: Promotion Becomes Punishment
angle-1.expansion: You championed a rep's promotion. Now the comp transition is broken, and they're questioning their first paycheck in the new role. That win you created just became your liability.

angle-1.label: Manual Is the System
angle-1.expansion: Every promotion triggers a one-off fix you have to build by hand. The process doesn't scale — and neither do you.

angle-1.label: The Math Owns You
angle-1.expansion: Every new hire joining mid-quarter means you're back in a spreadsheet, reverse-engineering a proration formula. The system didn't break — you just never had one.

angle-1.label: First Paycheck Is a Test
angle-1.expansion: A new rep's first commission check is when they decide if they trust comp. One ramp error and you've already lost them — before they've closed a single deal.

angle-1.label: Errors Surface Late
angle-1.expansion: Manual proration mistakes don't show up until a rep disputes their number at quarter-end. By then, you're not fixing a calculation — you're defending your process to the CRO.

angle-2.label: The Process Owns You
angle-2.expansion: Ramp schedules are supposed to run on autopilot. Instead, you're the human cron job — manually re-entering percentages every month so the math stays honest.

angle-2.label: One Miss, Full Blame
angle-2.expansion: If you forget to update a ramp tier mid-month, the rep's quota is wrong, their attainment is wrong, and you're the reason a new hire's first paycheck is a trust-breaker.

angle-2.label: Architect Reduced to Admin
angle-2.expansion: You designed the ramp structure. Now you spend your time executing it by hand — not because it's complex, but because the system won't do what you already decided.

angle-1.label: You Own Every Rounding Error
angle-1.expansion: When attainment has to be hand-split across two roles, the math is yours to defend. One disputed number and you're the one in the rep's Slack at 9pm explaining a spreadsheet.

angle-1.label: The Plan Lags the Business
angle-1.expansion: Leadership moved the rep. You're still reconciling who they used to be. The business already made the call — your system just hasn't caught up.

angle-2.label: Disputed Deals, Disputed Judgment
angle-2.expansion: When two reps both claim credit for the same closed deal, you're not just resolving a dispute — you're the one who drew the line, and now your call defines who trusts you.

angle-2.label: No Clean Answer, Only Your Answer
angle-2.expansion: There's no system of record for who touched what before the boundary moved. So every ruling is a judgment call — and judgment calls can always be wrong, publicly.
